USGS Astrogeology Science Center · NASA/MRO HiRISE · Mars 2020 TRN DTM mosaic (DOI 10.5066/P9REJ9JN) · Display-grade shaded elevation (hypsometric tint x analytic hillshade, sun 315 deg az / 45 deg alt, derived by team/jezero/terrain/build_terrain.mjs from the audited 1 m DTM), NOT the native 1 m posts and NOT a route-safety, hazard or engineering product. Vertical datum: areoid-relative meters, verified against the PLACES traverse (median DTM-PLACES offset +0.025 m, abs P95 4.3 m, 30,445 matched points; team/jezero/terrain/audit_terrain.mjs - all checks pass). Documented caveats: the far-west Jezero_CR stereo component (USGS-documented uncompensated y-parallax) carries a small positive bias (~+3 m mean, abs P95 ~4.9 m in the traverse bins crossing it); the FGDC published value range is understated - sampled values to -1639.971 m are real western-rim terrain confirmed by rover ground truth (PLACES sol 1354: -1786.0 m at 18.4575 N, 77.2685 E, matched within ~5 m). Ramp saturates at -2620/-1770 m (p2-p98 of the coverage); the display shares the region display-transform caveats (planetocentric display latitude on Web Mercator, pending the PPPCS ellipsoid review).

Coverage: USGS Mars 2020 TRN HiRISE DTM mosaic (JEZ_hirise_soc_006, 1 m/px, DOI 10.5066/P9REJ9JN) over the Jezero exploration area: derived shaded-elevation display tiles cover 77.2229-77.4931 E, 18.4020-18.5197 N (Web-Mercator XYZ, zooms 5-14, 193 RGBA tiles; tile ranges span the region extent, data only within the footprint). Pixels outside the DTM footprint - including the supported extent's west margin, 77.1868-77.2229 E - are transparent (no terrain data there).

USGS Astrogeology · NASA/MRO HiRISE · Mars 2020 TRN DTM (DOI 10.5066/P9REJ9JN); artificial illumination · Hillshade uses artificial illumination derived from elevation data to reveal terrain shape. It does not represent actual sunlight, surface temperature, or terrain safety. Surface-normal illumination, azimuth 315 degrees clockwise from north, elevation 45 degrees; 2m native map-coordinate gradient baseline with strict bilinear support and Mars ground-spacing correction. No cast shadows or gap filling. Fine relief can alias at coarse zooms. Independent absolute registration remains UNVERIFIED; the map remains limited to the mission view.

Coverage: Full native Jezero SOC_006 DEM envelope: 77.222933-77.583964 E, 18.306799-18.669315 N, with an irregular valid-data footprint. XYZ RGBA zooms 5-14. Nodata and unsupported gradient edges transparent; envelope is not a valid-data rectangle.

USGS Astrogeology Science Center · NASA/MRO HiRISE · derived from the Mars 2020 TRN DTM mosaic (DOI 10.5066/P9REJ9JN) · Derived display measurement, not a hazard or trafficability product: slope = atan(sqrt((dz/dx)^2 + (dz/dy)^2)) computed by team/jezero/terrain/build_slope.mjs on the display pixel grid from bilinearly sampled DTM elevations, with Mars ground spacing (r = 3,396,190 m). The measurement baseline is therefore the display pixel size, not the native 1 m post: ~10 m at z14, ~19 m at z13, ~150 m at z10 and ~5 km at z5, so low zooms show a smoothed regional gradient and the same terrain reads slightly gentler as zoom decreases. Slope alone says nothing about bearing strength, rock abundance, sand trapping or rover trafficability; unknown terrain is not safe terrain. Vertical-datum caveats and the far-west CR stereo bias (~3-5 m) documented for the Elevation layer apply to the underlying elevations; the display shares the region display-transform caveats (planetocentric display latitude on Web Mercator).

Coverage: Slope derived from the same USGS Mars 2020 TRN HiRISE DTM mosaic (JEZ_hirise_soc_006, 1 m/px, DOI 10.5066/P9REJ9JN): display tiles cover 77.2229-77.4931 E, 18.4020-18.5197 N (Web-Mercator XYZ, zooms 5-14, 193 RGBA tiles; tile ranges span the region extent, data only within the footprint). Pixels outside the DTM footprint - including the west margin 77.1868-77.2229 E - are transparent (no terrain data there).

NASA/JPL · Arizona State University · THEMIS daytime IR controlled mosaic v2 · NASA Mars Trek · Relative daytime infrared brightness only (qualitative): the mosaic ships no verified radiometric scaling, so no temperature, thermal-inertia, rock-abundance or dust-cover values are asserted - the legend deliberately has no units. Daytime IR mixes albedo and thermophysical properties, so bright/dark patches are not by themselves a compositional or hazard classification. Not a thermal-inertia product: the TES inertia map (3 km/px) is far too coarse for this region and is not used. Display-grade: tiles nearest-neighbour resampled 1:1 from source level L=z-1 by team/jezero/basemap/prepare_trek_basemap.mjs; the ~100 m source is upsampled above z9. Source alpha is preserved. The display shares the region display-transform caveats (planetocentric display latitude on Web Mercator).

Coverage: THEMIS daytime infrared controlled mosaic v2 (Oct 2018, ~100 m/px) over the Jezero exploration area: derived display tiles cover 77.137-77.543 E, 18.352-18.570 N (Web-Mercator XYZ, zooms 5-9; above z9 the renderer upsamples the same source).
